content:
The law operates like a rigid natal chart  forcing messy human reality onto a flat grid of ancient statutes. If your life falls outside its narrow degrees, it pathologizes you as an error.
This mirrors the scholastic gatekeepers of Banaras who used rigid dogmas to calculate who was worthy. Modern legal formalism runs on the same fatalistic delusion: it casts trauma as a bad transit, penalizes raw emotion, and worships fixed precedent out of terror.
